audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read Skill for rows 0-5 and Yasuo for row 6, while the content layer and packet chart read Karma/Karma/Karma/Skill/Yasuo/Yasuo/Karma. Every row except the Levels 4-5 row disagreed across layers, including the late row, where the page said Yasuo wins while its own prose said Karma out-values him.
audit.why: Steel Tempest reaches 475 and needs a third stack to knock up, so Karma's 950 Q owns levels 1-3. Last Breath at 70s and crit items give Yasuo levels 6 through one item. Late, Karma's Mantra-E and root utility beat his single-target burst — which is what whys[6] and spikes[3] already said.
audit.corrected: Full-layer rows aligned to the content layer: 0-2 Karma, 3 Skill, 4-5 Yasuo, 6 Karma, with every why rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike prose used 'windwall' as a common noun and never stated Last Breath's cooldown or Wind Wall's duration.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17s and lasts 4 seconds; Last Breath is 70/50/30s. Those numbers are what make the advice actionable.
audit.corrected: spikes[0], spikes[2] and mid rewritten with the real name and the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction — Wind Wall blocks Inner Flame and Mantra-Q but not the targeted Focused Resolve tether — was stated only in the tldr and never in the trading, cooldown, or do/don't fields. breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it (lintFindings COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: Karma's Q carries the 'projectile — can be blocked by Wind Wall-class effects' flag; her W is a targeted tether and her E a targeted shield, so neither is stopped by the wall. Wind Wall is up 4 seconds on a 25s rank-1 cooldown, which leaves 21 seconds of free poke.
audit.corrected: tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0] now state wall-proof W, the 4-second block, and the 21-second gap.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood line pasted under 'RE-speed the disengage window'; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad under 'Trade extended past your root' (both lintFindings COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: Sweeping Blade is a 0.5s dash at rank 1 with no cost, so the moment your root ends he is mobile again.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to match their titles, keyed to Sweeping Blade's 0.5s and Last Breath's 70s.

edits.before: No new ult — your 6 is a Mantra rank: faster cycles, bigger RQs. Press the early lead before scaling lanes wake up.

edits.before: Blackfire/Luden's spike: RQ-W chains threaten kills outright. The lane is now or never — you fall off politely.

edits.before: Late Karma is a utility engine: RE shields the team, W roots the diver, and RQ pokes the objective setup.
edits.after: Late Karma is the utility engine: RE the engage, W-root him through Wind Wall, and RQ the siege from 950.

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Yasuo wins by eating your Q in Wind Wall for 4 seconds, then blinking onto a knockup with Last Breath.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Count it out loud if you must. - Your RE shield-speed has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Yasuo Wind Wall: 25s at rank 1, 17s maxed, 4 seconds of blocked projectiles — your Q and Mantra-Q die in it, your targeted W tether does not. - Sweeping Blade is a 0.5s dash and costs nothing. - Last Breath is 70s at rank 1 and 30s maxed.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, and on real windows RQ-W: the chunk plus tether-root turns a poke trade into a kill setup — E out before the answer.
edits.after: W-tether him through the wall — it is targeted, not a projectile — then RQ once the 4 seconds run out and E yourself out.

edits.before: Spending Mantra on wave-clear while behind on poke — Karma without RQ banked is a support who took mid's farm.

edits.before: Your tether breaks if YOU walk away — holding the root means holding your ground for two seconds you must plan for.
edits.after: If the Mantra-E shield carries you through Last Breath, that is worth more than the extra Q damage ever was.

edits.before: Spending Mantra on wave-clear while behind on poke — Karma without RQ banked is a support who took mid's farm.
edits.after: Once the root ends he has Sweeping Blade and Steel Tempest back — leave on your E speed, do not stay to duel.

edits.before: Yasuo's Steel Tempest procs need minion knockups he doesn't have yet, so your Inner Flame range and Inspire shield let you poke him down safely before his windwall can block your key combos.
edits.after: Steel Tempest reaches only 475 and needs a third stack to knock up, so Inner Flame at 950 and the Inspire shield poke him down before Wind Wall exists at level 3 to block anything.

edits.after: With crit items online, Yasuo's all-in burst and a Wind Wall that eats your Mantra-Q start winning skirmishes decisively, especially with a knockup from his jungler or his own third Steel Tempest.
